Subject: Light Up a Life 2026 — draft for Moira to review

Hilary asked on the page whether we are doing the tree again this year. Yes, we are, Hilary, and we shall be very pleased to see you and your sister. Our Light Up a Life tree will be back in the bookshop window this November, with room for the names of people we miss.

It is seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree, I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen. I still have to stop for a moment, but it has become something I am glad to do, among the ordinary comings and goings of the shop.

I mention that because I know coming in to write a name can be harder than it sounds. There is no need to explain yourself, or to find anything particularly fine to say. And the tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only for families who have been cared for by the hospice. Whether this is your first Christmas without someone or you have been missing them for many years, you are very welcome.

Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take yours home and write it there. Some things are easier at your own kitchen table, and others are easier with a little company.

We shall switch on the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is making mince pies again. Those who came last year will remember that the children sang beautifully and the mince pies disappeared remarkably quickly.

All the names on the tags will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your loved one’s name to be read.

Thank you to everyone who helped fill last year’s tree with 412 names, and to everyone who came along, sang, listened or stood quietly with us. I remember the kindness of that evening as much as anything.

You are welcome to come and stand by the tree without writing a tag, too. You need not buy a book or anything else. Much as we usually encourage a rummage through the shelves, this is one occasion when you need not have any reason to come in beyond wanting to be there.

Jean
